scholarships.title: KAIST Scholarship (KAIST International Graduate Admission)
scholarships.official_source: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), Office of Admissions

existing.description: KAIST's own scholarship for international graduate students, selected as part of the admission application rather than as a separate scholarship application. It covers full tuition fees plus national health insurance and a monthly stipend, and 94% of KAIST's international student body receive it. Two higher tiers are awarded automatically to those selected: the KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship (KRW 1,000,000 per month for 4 regular semesters) and the KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KRW 300,000 per month for 8 regular semesters). The published cost-of-study table shows the student still carries on-campus housing, food, books, travel and telecommunications costs.
eligibility: Applicants must be citizens of countries other than Korea; individuals holding Korean citizenship are not eligible

Applicants of Korean descent who hold foreign citizenship must submit official documentation confirming the renunciation of Korean citizenship for both the applicant and their parents, completed prior to the start of the application period with supporting academic records, or must have completed their entire primary and secondary education (Grades 1 through 12) outside of Korea with certified graduation certificates and transcripts covering all years
Bachelor's degree or equivalent standard by the start of the course for the Master's or Master's-Ph.D. degree program application
Master's degree or equivalent standard by the start of the course for the Ph.D. degree program application
At least one published English proficiency test score (TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, TOEIC or TEPS), valid as of the online application deadline
Departments accepting KAIST Scholarship applications: all departments except the Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track)
Admission Periods: Spring / Fall Early / Fall Regular
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to international applicants for KAIST graduate programmes who are citizens of countries other than Korea, hold a bachelor's degree (master's/Master's-Ph.D.) or a master's degree (Ph.D.) by the start of the course, and provide a qualifying English proficiency test score unless a published exemption applies.
benefits: KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship (KGPS): full tuition coverage and a monthly stipend of 1,000,000 KRW for 4 regular semesters, for Master's or Master's-Ph.D. Integrated applicants

KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KPS): full tuition coverage and a monthly stipend of 300,000 KRW for 8 regular semesters, for Master's-Ph.D. Integrated or Ph.D. applicants
Research opportunities that KAIST states enable most students to achieve financial self-sufficiency
Full tuition coverage and guaranteed minimum living expenses (stated on the Cost of Studying at KAIST page for students admitted with the KAIST Scholarship)
requirements: Select the KAIST scholarship option in the admission application; if eligible, accepted candidates are automatically considered for the KGPS or KPS
No separate application is necessary for the KGPS
Submitted through KAIST's ApplyWeb online application system
Provide a recommendation letter through KAIST's separate online Letter of Recommendation system for graduate applicants
documents: Recommendation letter submitted through the KAIST online Letter of Recommendation system for graduate applicants
existing.english_requirement: KAIST's official language of communication and instruction for international students is English. All applicants must provide at least one English proficiency test score, and the scores must be valid as of the online application deadline. Published minimums: TOEFL iBT 83 (taken before 21 Jan 2026) or 4.5 (taken on or after 21 Jan 2026); IELTS Academic 6.5 band; TOEIC 720 (Listening & Reading, TOEIC Public Testing Program); TEPS 326. TOEFL institutional code 0195, department code 99; Home Edition accepted; iBT MyBest Scores are NOT accepted; IELTS Online is accepted but IELTS One Skill Retake is NOT accepted; test scores from Institutional Testing Program (ITP) are NOT accepted. Exemption: no EPT score is required if you hold citizenship of, or have physically studied and completed a bachelor's-equivalent or higher qualification at an institution physically located in, Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Malta, New Zealand, St Kitts, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad and Tobago, the U.K. or the U.S.A. A further exemption applies if you hold citizenship of one of a listed group of countries AND have physically studied and completed a qualification equivalent to a bachelor's degree or higher in English as the medium of instruction at an institution physically located in one of those countries, in which case a certificate from the school attended indicating English as the medium of instruction (e.g. English Lecture Certificate) must additionally be provided. Applicants expecting to graduate from regular KAIST degree programmes in the semester before the intended course also do not need to provide a score. Programs that do not require an EPT score: GDI-ITTP track, KINS-KAIST.
application_method: Check the published admission window for your entry term (Spring: mid August - early September; Fall Early: early December - late December; Fall Regular: early March - late March)
Create an ApplyWeb account and complete the KAIST International Graduate online application
Select the KAIST scholarship option as your financial resource in the application
Request your recommendation letter through the KAIST online Letter of Recommendation system during the designated submission period
Submit the application before the online application deadline (the EPT score must be valid as of that deadline)
If selected, you are automatically considered for the KGPS and/or KPS; no separate scholarship application is needed
Respond to the offer, register for school, prepare the certificate of admission and apply for a student visa
existing.selection_notes: Scholarship status is decided inside the admission process: applicants who select the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource in the application are automatically considered for the KAIST Scholarship and, where the degree programme matches, for the KGPS or the KPS. For the KGPS, no separate application is made and only highly competitive applicants will be recommended by the department head. For the KPS, applicants demonstrating outstanding academic and research achievements receive recommendations from the department head, with final selection by the college dean. KAIST states that 94 percent of its international students benefit from the scholarship and that the scholarship rate may vary by student.
existing.best_fit: Non-Korean nationals applying to KAIST master's, Master's-Ph.D. integrated or Ph.D. programmes who meet KAIST's English proficiency requirement (or a published exemption) and can satisfy a doctoral or master's-level qualification by the start of the course.
existing.notes: Not a standalone scholarship application: the award is attached to admission. The monthly stipend of the base KAIST Scholarship is stated to be dependent on research involvement, and no base stipend figure is published; KAIST also states the stipend amount may vary depending on individual colleges, with the College of Engineering publishing its own stipend terms separately. The KPS stipend for Master's-Ph.D. integrated entrants begins at the start of the Ph.D. programme, not on entry. The published Cost of Studying at KAIST figures are for the 2023 academic year. The Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track) is excluded from KAIST Scholarship applications.
existing.application_period: The 2027 Spring Semester international-track window (2026/08/18 - 2026/09/01) has closed. The next published window is Fall Admission (Early Track), Early December - Late December; the Fall 2027 Entry dates are published as TBA on the official timeline page.
existing.deadline_display: KAIST International Graduate Admission general windows: Spring Admission: Mid August - Early September; Fall Admission (Early Track): Early December - Late December; Fall Admission (Regular Track): Early March - Late March. Published 2027-entry dates: Spring 2027 Entry: August 18 - September 1, 2026; Fall 2027 Entry: TBA.

scholarships.title: KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KPS)
scholarships.official_source: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

existing.description: The KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KPS) is one of two named awards inside the KAIST Scholarship scheme for international graduate students, the other being the KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship (KGPS). KAIST's Office of Admissions states that KPS is open to international applicants in Master's-Ph.D. Integrated or Ph.D. programmes in all departments and provides full tuition coverage plus a monthly stipend of 300,000 KRW for eight regular semesters. Applicants are considered automatically for KPS by selecting the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource in the admission application; candidates with outstanding academic and research achievements are recommended by the department head and selected by the college dean.
eligibility: International applicant (citizen of a country other than Korea) for a KAIST graduate programme
Applying to a Master's-Ph.D. Integrated or Ph.D. programme
Selected the KAIST scholarship as the financial resource in the admission application
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to international applicants for KAIST Master's-Ph.D. Integrated or Ph.D. programmes in any department. There is no separate KPS application: candidates are considered automatically if they select the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource in the KAIST international graduate admission application.
benefits: Master's-Ph.D. Integrated entrants receive the scholarship from the start of the Ph.D. programme
documents: KAIST international graduate admission application form
Statement of Financial Resources with 'KAIST Scholarship' selected (no bank statements required if KAIST Scholarship is the only option selected)
Official transcripts and degree certificates from previous institutions
English proficiency test score (KAIST states an EPT score is required unless a waiver/exemption applies)
existing.english_requirement: KAIST states an English proficiency test score is required for international applicants unless a waiver or country exemption applies; the exact accepted tests and minimum scores are published on its Eligibility Requirements page, which was not fetched for this record.
existing.duration: 8 regular semesters of support (from the start of the Ph.D. programme for Master's-Ph.D. Integrated entrants)
existing.application_period: Three annual admission periods (Spring, Fall Early, Fall Regular). Spring 2027 entry applications ran 18 Aug - 1 Sep 2026; Fall 2027 entry dates are still listed as TBA.
existing.deadline_display: No separate scholarship deadline - KPS follows KAIST International Graduate Admission periods, listed officially as 'Spring/Fall Early/Fall Regular'. For 2027 entries KAIST publishes 'Spring 2027 Entry: August 18 - September 1, 2026' and 'Fall 2027 Entry: TBA'.
existing.program_type: Graduate scholarship for international doctoral students, awarded automatically within the KAIST Scholarship scheme
